name: write_text_via_dos
description: Returns at once when a control word is zero. Otherwise it measures a null-terminated string at the address in the A0 register and sends it through the DOS write call via a stored function pointer.

name: conditionally_flush_cpu_caches
description: Calls a library routine through a pointer read at a fixed offset when a word in a structure exceeds a threshold, then calls a second library routine. The listed library calls are the exec cache-control and supervisor routines.

name: write_dma_and_interrupt_control
description: Writes to the DMA control and interrupt enable registers, where bit 15 of the written value selects enable or disable. The decompiler produced no body, so only the register use and call relations are recovered.

name: pass_control_to_routine
description: A two-instruction routine that only passes control on to one other routine. The decompiler produced no body, so this is recovered from its call relations alone.

name: set_background_color_and_dma
description: Writes the background color register and the DMA and interrupt enable registers, and calls three other routines. The decompiler produced no body, so the order of the writes is not recovered.

name: setup_imp_marker_and_hardware
description: Refers to the text IMP! and touches two custom hardware registers, and calls three other routines. The decompiler produced no body, so the exact steps are not recovered.

name: select_and_copy_loader_image
description: Checks a byte in a header and branches to one of two paths: one copies a block of longwords to a fixed destination, the other matches a name against a table, uppercases a string, copies a larger block and patches words according to a flag. The routine also refers to the text IMP!.

name: copy_block_and_patch_jump
description: Copies a block of longwords to a fixed destination, calls one routine, then writes words chosen by the bits of a flag, followed by a jump-style word and a routine address. It also refers to the text IMP!.

name: reset_cia_serial_interrupt_state
description: If a flag bit is set, it sets another bit, calls one routine and clears that bit again. It then stores a fixed value and touches the CIA-A control and interrupt registers and the interrupt request register.

name: send_keyboard_serial_sequence
description: Calls one routine, then repeatedly writes two fixed byte values to the keyboard serial register, waiting on a status bit after each write. The register note identifies the target as the keyboard serial register.

name: update_key_state_from_byte
description: Updates a 16-bit state word from one input byte: certain specific byte values set the state or XOR it with fixed constants, and the state is then replaced by a bit-rotated form of the inverted byte. It is called by one routine.

name: install_header_routine_and_copy
description: Stores a routine address and a byte from a header structure, uppercases a string, searches a table, copies a block of longwords and then calls one routine. It is called by three routines.

name: copy_matched_table_block
description: Searches a table of entries by comparing bytes of a name, copies a block of longwords for the matched entry, then calls one routine. The routine also refers to the text IMP!.

name: copy_longword_block_to_destination
description: Looks up a source offset from a table entry, copies longwords to a destination until the source end is reached, then calls one routine.

name: unpack_imp_packed_data
description: Checks for the IMP! magic word and, when it matches, unpacks the packed data backwards by reading a bit stream and copying runs of bytes. The listing is truncated, so the other path is not recovered.

name: install_temporary_interrupt_handler
description: Saves a few system values, clears a block of longwords, installs an interrupt handler routine, and waits in a loop on a flag before restoring the saved values. It uses the supervisor call and the interrupt enable register.

name: open_graphics_and_reset_hardware
description: Opens the graphics library by name and closes it again, and writes to the audio, DMA and interrupt control registers, including the copper location registers. It calls a routine that clears the audio DMA channels and five other routines; the decompiler body is empty, so the steps come from the listed facts.

name: read_masked_interrupt_request_bits
description: Reads the interrupt request register, masks the result with a fixed bit pattern and stores it in a global variable. It is called by one routine.

name: run_next_nonempty_table_handler
description: Steps a stored index backwards through a table in eight-byte steps until it finds a non-empty entry, calls that entry as a routine, and advances the index by one entry when the result is non-zero.

name: adjust_word_nibbles_toward_target
description: Walks two arrays of 16-bit words together and increments each word of the first array in steps of 1, 16 or 256 until each nibble matches the second array. It loops until a counter register wraps past zero.

name: decrement_word_nibbles_toward_target
description: Walks two arrays of 16-bit words together and decrements each word of the first array in steps of 1, 16 or 256 until each nibble matches the second array. It loops until a counter register reaches minus one.

name: run_input_state_machine
description: Runs a small input state machine that uses counters, bit toggles and comparisons, and reads the fire button, mouse movement and right and middle button registers. It refers to the text strings NO and YES and calls seven other routines.

name: stub_single_instruction_entry
description: A one-instruction entry whose decompiled body is identical to the routine that follows it, so the decompiler output is unreliable at this address. Only its single caller and its address-taken reference are recovered.

name: update_mouse_position_counter
description: Clamps a counter between zero and a fixed maximum, stores a shifted copy of it in a byte, and writes a fixed word pattern to a small block with one indexed word replaced. The register note lists the mouse movement register, and the routine calls four other routines.

name: copy_text_glyphs_if_pending
description: Converts each character of a text string into eight-row glyph columns copied from a font table into a bitplane buffer, moving to a new line after a fixed number of characters. It skips the copy when a completion flag is already set, and sets that flag afterwards.

name: copy_text_glyphs_when_idle
description: If a state byte is not already one, it sets it and, unless a completion flag is set, copies the glyph columns for each character of the text string into a buffer. It then sets the completion flag.

name: copy_text_glyphs_to_buffer
description: Copies the glyph columns for each character of a null-terminated text string into a buffer, moving to a new line after a fixed number of characters. It sets a completion flag when the string ends.

name: advance_frame_counter_and_fill
description: Increments a counter and, once it passes three, calls another routine, copies a few global words, writes a block of words from a global value and increments a byte counter. It then resets the first counter.

name: fill_block_and_increment_counter
description: Calls one routine, copies a few global words, writes four words from a global value into a block, and increments a global counter.

name: open_cia_resources_and_libraries
description: Opens the named resources b.resource and ciab.resource and the graphics library, and closes the library again, touching the port registers of both CIA chips along the way. The decompiler timed out, so the order of the steps is only partly recovered.

name: call_library_offset_entry
description: Calls one library function through a fixed jump-table offset and is called by two routines. The decompiler timed out, so only that call relation is recovered.

name: build_linked_slot_table
description: Scans a byte table until a terminating value, then builds a set of linked slots by zeroing words and storing pointers to them, and finally sets flag bits and clears several words. It also touches the CIA-A port register.

name: copy_four_table_entry_words
description: Copies four words from a table entry to the destination, replacing the sentinel minus two with minus one, and stores the count of valid copies in the next word. It clears a global flag.

key: cruise for a corpse (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr skr](disk 1 of 5)[a]/Cruise for a Corpse (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 5)[a].adf:Skid_Row_Cracked_Cruise:0:0068
name: copy_three_table_entry_words
description: Writes a minus one word, then copies three table words the same way, replacing the sentinel with minus one, and stores the count of valid copies in the following word. It clears a global flag.

name: copy_two_table_entry_words
description: Writes a minus one word, copies two table words with the same sentinel handling, and stores the count of valid copies in the following word. It clears a global flag.

key: cruise for a corpse (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr skr](disk 1 of 5)[a]/Cruise for a Corpse (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 5)[a].adf:Skid_Row_Cracked_Cruise:0:008C
name: copy_one_table_entry_word
description: Writes a minus one word, copies one table word with the same sentinel handling, and stores the count in the following word. It clears a global flag.

key: cruise for a corpse (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr skr](disk 1 of 5)[a]/Cruise for a Corpse (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 5)[a].adf:Skid_Row_Cracked_Cruise:0:009E
name: store_sentinel_and_count_word
description: Writes a minus one word, clears a global flag and stores the input register value in the following word. It is called by two routines.

name: call_library_entry
description: At program entry it calls one routine, and if the zero flag is clear it calls a second routine and then a function pointer taken from a table. It then calls a third routine before returning.

description: Calls the exec OldOpenLibrary entry through a library table pointer and stores the returned handle in a global variable. It refers to the text dos.library.

description: If a destination pointer is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a table at a fixed offset into it, then calls one routine through a stored pointer.

description: Unpacks a block backwards into memory by reading bits from a stream and copying byte runs and literal bytes until the destination reaches its start. It calls a flag-test routine and three other routines.

name: shift_bit_buffer_with_extend
description: Repeatedly shifts a bit buffer by a count held in a register, carrying bits through the extend flag and refilling from input words when the buffer empties. It calls a flag-test routine, a subtraction routine and two other routines.

name: allocate_and_copy_entry_block
description: Program entry that scans a chain of table entries for the largest value, writes an incrementing sequence of longwords into a newly allocated block, and copies a block of longwords into another area. It returns minus one when a required call fails and zero otherwise.

name: clear_block_and_dispatch_result
description: Calls one routine, clears a block of 25 longwords and stores values from a global table into it. It then calls a library entry, and when the result is zero it calls a second entry, otherwise it calls one other routine.

key: cruise for a corpse (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr skr](disk 1 of 5)[a]/Cruise for a Corpse (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 5)[a].adf:add21k:0:0004

description: Opens the dos, graphics and intuition libraries by name, showing an alert if one fails to open. It then reads fields from the opened structures, calls library entries in a loop, and closes the libraries again.

description: Allocates a record and fills its fields. When a stored flag is clear it opens the DOS current directory, input and output and stores their handles in the record; otherwise it sets flag bits in the record and calls one routine.

key: cruise for a corpse (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr skr](disk 1 of 5)[a]/Cruise for a Corpse (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 5)[a].adf:add21k:0:0362
name: split_command_line_into_tokens
description: Copies a string into a buffer while splitting it into tokens at whitespace, honoring double quotes and doubled quotes, and stores a pointer to each token in an allocated table ending with a null pointer. It stores the token count in a global variable.

description: Opens the icon library by name and, when that succeeds, calls library entries to obtain values that are stored in fields of a record, then releases the library. The routine also refers to the text WINDOW and calls dos.Open.

name: close_indexed_dos_handle
description: Returns minus one and sets an error code when the index is out of range or the entry is empty. Otherwise it closes the DOS handle in that entry unless a flag bit is set, clears the entry and returns zero.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: A two-instruction routine that returns minus one. It is reached from outside the static flow, and its only recovered behaviour is that return value.

name: stub_return_only
description: Its decompiled body only returns. The listed facts show the fire-button port register as touched, but that access is not recovered from the body.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a table at a fixed offset into it, then calls one routine through a stored pointer.

name: setup_graphics_and_launch_code
description: Program entry that opens the graphics library by name, waits for the vertical blank, and sets the display, interrupt and DMA control registers. It checks available memory and memory type through library calls, delays in loops, and then transfers control to a fixed address. The listing also calls five other routines.

name: set_bitmask_range_bits
description: Sets one bit in a global word for each index from a starting value up to a computed end, then returns the input register value. It is called by one routine.

name: pass_control_to_routine
description: A single-instruction routine that passes control on to one other routine. The decompiler timed out, so only that call relation is recovered.

name: invoke_small_setup_and_routine
description: Calls a four-instruction routine and one other routine, and is referenced by three routines and by a handler pointer in data. The decompiler timed out, so the sequence of its steps is not recovered.

name: build_four_entry_descriptor_table
description: Walks four table entries, storing for each one a pointer, an address offset adjusted by the base value when its top bit is set, and a length found by scanning for a pair of marker words. A second loop checks a flag bit in each entry and calls one routine for entries where that bit is clear.

name: build_copper_list_entry_table
description: Builds a table of four entries, storing a pointer, an offset and a length for each, then runs a second pass that calls a routine for entries whose flag bit is clear and sets a global pointer. The listed facts also show the copper location and jump registers and the DMA control register being touched.

name: copy_bytes_handling_overlap
description: Copies a block of bytes from one address to another, moving forward when the destination is below the source and backward otherwise, so overlapping blocks are handled. The count is taken from a register.

name: unpack_tagged_bitstream_rows
description: If a magic longword matches, it copies a header block, then unpacks bit-coded runs of bytes into a buffer and rearranges that buffer into rows of 52 bytes. It calls three other routines, and the decompiler output is only partly recovered.

name: decode_huffman_symbol
description: Reads bits from a packed stream and walks a table of code limits until the accumulated code falls within one, then returns the matching symbol from a second table. It refills the bit buffer through a routine.

name: decode_huffman_symbol_bits
description: A variant of the bit-stream symbol decoder: it shifts bits into a code value, compares it against a table of limits, and returns the symbol from a second table when a limit is reached. The listed facts show one other routine being called.

name: mask_low_bits_of_value
description: Returns the input word masked to the low bits given by a count in a register, using one shifted left by that count minus one as the mask. It is called by three routines.

name: build_decode_lookup_tables
description: Reads a set of symbol counts through a routine into an array, zero-fills the rest of a section, and then builds accumulated code limits and offsets in the structure. The listing calls other routines for each step.

name: read_symbols_into_lookup_table
description: Reads a count and a list of symbol values through a routine into an array, then builds accumulated code limits and offsets in the structure. It calls two other routines.

name: build_code_limit_table
description: Copies a run of words from a routine into a table, then derives accumulated code limits and offsets from a source array and stores them in the structure. It calls one other routine.

name: copy_stub_to_low_memory
description: Entry point that copies a block of 32 words from the routine named EMPIRE into low memory at address 224, then returns.

name: patch_words_and_call_target
description: Writes a longword and a word at fixed offsets of a table, then calls through the base pointer of that table. The decompiler could not recover the jump table, so the target is not identified.

name: save_system_state_and_quiesce
description: Checks the chip revision bits and, when the graphics library is found, saves some of its system values after waiting for the display. It then clears a block of hardware register longwords, optionally writes a few display registers, and calls a routine that reads the vector base register.

name: read_vector_base_register
description: Reads the vector base register through the exec Supervisor call when the CPU-type flag is set, and stores the result at the address held in a register. When the flag is clear the stored value is zero. It is called by the system-state routine.

name: run_text_fade_sequence
description: Returns unless a flag bit is set, then loops while waiting for the display frame and calls routines that build text and fade it in and out. It finishes by waiting for the frames to complete and calling a final routine before returning. The listed facts also show the fire-button register being read.

name: advance_toggle_and_refill_slots
description: Toggles a flag word and, each time it returns to zero, advances a counter and writes a value from a global word into three entries spaced eight words apart.

name: toggle_and_clear_three_slots
description: Toggles a flag word and, when it reaches zero, decrements a counter and writes a value from a global word into three entries spaced eight words apart, but only while the counter stays non-negative.

name: unpack_compressed_table
description: Calls a routine 32 times, then iterates over a table of 32 words, splitting each word into four-bit nibbles and storing them with their negated values into a destination structure. It references a table named FLT_LOGO.

name: find_max_nibble_value
description: Scans the four nibbles of a 16-bit word and keeps the largest one in a register. It runs exactly four times, once per four-bit segment.

name: update_nibble_counters_table
description: Once a countdown reaches zero it resets the countdown to four, then walks 32 table entries: nonzero counts are decremented, and zero counts are adjusted by a weighted nibble mask when it differs from a stored value.

name: decrement_nonzero_nibbles_table
description: Once a countdown reaches zero it resets it to four, then walks table entries and reduces each non-zero nibble of every entry by one, skipping one entry at a fixed position on the first pass.

name: install_handlers_and_setup_hardware
description: Saves the system variables, replaces two system vector entries with local handler routines, and calls the saved-state routine. It then runs the table unpacking and table setup routines, writes to the CIA and video control registers, and sets up four audio channel records with fixed values.

name: initialise_copper_pointer_tables
description: Fills four pointer entries from a base address with a fixed stride, each addressing a display plane register, then writes 80 words of increasing values, each followed by a zero word, into a second table. It also stores two fixed words in a structure.

name: restore_saved_system_state
description: Restores the saved system variables, writes interrupt and display values from saved globals, and calls routines through the library table. It finishes with a tail call to the system-state routine.

name: set_intreq_values
description: Writes the constant 255 to one variable and 32 to a global variable, which the listed facts associate with the interrupt request register. It is called from the system setup routine.

name: set_cia_intreq_bits
description: Writes the constant 255 to one variable and 8192 to a global variable, configuring the CIA interrupt control state. It is called from the system setup routine.

name: render_text_into_bitmap
description: Clears a block of longwords for a text bitmap, then draws each line of a text string into it using font glyph bytes, moving to the next line on a newline or control code. It stops at the end of the string or after 14 lines.

name: render_text_into_bitmap
